Padding must bypass recurrence: a zero embedding alone does not prevent GRU biases and recurrent gates from changing hidden states. Implementation implication of the [PyTorch GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html): use a GRUCell loop with `h = torch.where(valid[:, None], cell(x, h), h)` at every layer, or remove left padding, right-pad the resulting valid sequences, and pack them before the GRU. Packing assumes valid prefixes; passing left-padded tensors with their nonzero counts would process padding and truncate real items. Handle empty histories separately. See the [PyTorch packing example](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence.html).

For independently sampled subsequences or cropped suffixes, initialize every sample’s hidden state to zero; detaching a previous state preserves its information and therefore does not provide a fresh start. Construct aligned next-item pairs first, then crop input, positive targets, negatives and loss masks using identical positions: output after item `i_t` predicts `i_{t+1}`. Exclude padded inputs and missing targets from loss. For original left-padded outputs, gather the maximum index whose input is nonpadding—normally `L-1`, never `nonzero_count-1`. After internal compaction, restore outputs to original positions for `log2feats`, or explicitly map indices. These are implementation deductions from the sequence layout and GRU output semantics.

Stateful training requires chronological continuation within each batch slot: retain hidden values only for the same continuing history, detach at truncated-backpropagation boundaries, and reset when replacing a history. Original GRU4Rec uses session-parallel input/next-item pairs and resets the corresponding state when a session ends; random crops lack that continuity. See the [authors’ implementation analysis](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/third_party_recsys23.pdf). Diagnostics and inference must reproduce the chosen reset, padding and readout behavior.
